title: DECA: A Near-Core LLM Decompression Accelerator Grounded on a 3D Roofline Model
problem: LLM inference on CPU servers (Intel Sapphire Rapids with AMX TMUL and HBM) is bottlenecked not by memory bandwidth or matrix compute throughput, but by AVX vector decompression overhead: decompressing quantized (BF8, MXFP4) and sparsified weight tiles in software consumes over 95% of dynamic instructions per core, and even 4x more vector (AVX) throughput is insufficient to eliminate this bottleneck for highly compressed models.
motivation: CPU servers are an increasingly attractive LLM inference platform due to AMX matrix engines and HBM, but the inability of the traditional 2D roofline model to expose the vector-decompression bottleneck makes it unclear how to improve the system; a principled model-driven hardware solution is needed.
method: DECA is a hardware accelerator integrated next to each CPU core that unpacks compressed weights (quantized down to 1-8 bits and sparsified with zeros removed). It has three stages: lookup tables convert quantized values to full size (BF16), parallel prefix sum computes where zeros should go from a bitmask and controls a crossbar to restore them, and per-group scale factors are applied. Crucially, the CPU speculatively invokes DECA (via a TEPL instruction) without blocking—like requesting data speculatively from a cache—and since DECA never writes to memory, abandoned speculations are safe. Two register pairs buffer outputs so DECA can work on the next batch while the CPU reads the current one.
key_novelty: A 3D roofline model (adding a vector-throughput axis to the traditional 2D roofline) that correctly identified decompression—not memory bandwidth or compute—as the bottleneck for highly compressed models, directly enabling the design of DECA and its TEPL ISA extension, which speculatively invoke decompression without per-iteration memory fences.
contributions: The Roof-Surface 3D analytical performance model (and its 2D BORD projection) that correctly attributes compressed GeMM inefficiency to AVX vector throughput rather than memory bandwidth for HBM systems.

DECA near-core accelerator with a three-stage (dequantization-via-LUT/expansion-via-XBAR/scaling) pipeline supporting 1–8 bit quantization, arbitrary unstructured sparsity, and group quantization; achieves up to 4x speedup over libxsmm on compressed GeMMs.
TEPL ISA extension enabling out-of-order, speculative DECA invocation without per-iteration memory fences, hiding CPU-DECA communication latency and enabling cross-iteration overlap.
Reduction of next-token generation time for Llama2-70B and OPT-66B by 1.6x–2.6x over software-only and 2.5x–5.0x over uncompressed baseline in simulated 56-core SPR with HBM.

metrics.speedup: up to 4x over Intel libxsmm software kernels on compressed GeMMs; 1.6x–2.6x reduction in next-token generation time for Llama2-70B/OPT-66B vs software-only; 2.5x–5.0x vs uncompressed baseline
metrics.other: Roof-Surface model accurate to within 10% for most kernels; libxsmm BF8_5% density achieves only 1/4.94 of roofline-predicted optimal on HBM

baselines: uncompressed BF16 baseline on SPR DDR5/HBM
limitations: DECA is evaluated via simulation of a 56-core SPR system; no silicon measurements are provided, and the analysis focuses on generation-phase (low arithmetic intensity) inference with small batch sizes where weight bandwidth dominates, not prompt-phase or large-batch inference.
primary_theme: Near-core decompression accelerator for compressed LLM inference on CPU+HBM
